current_example.title: Example: Differentiating Hyperbolic Functions Using the Quotient Rule

q-95674.name: Question 1
q-95674.worked_solution:
First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic hyperbolic functions:

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sinh}⁡x)=\operatorname{cosh}⁡x,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x)={sech}^{2}⁡x
$$

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sinh}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sinh}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cosh}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

q-95674.html:
Question 1
?

Find the derivative of y=14sinh⁡x.

a
14tanh⁡x
b
−14cosh⁡x
c
−14sech⁡x
d
14sech⁡x
e
14cosh⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic hyperbolic functions:

ddx(sinh⁡x)=cosh⁡x,ddx(cosh⁡x)=sinh⁡x,ddx(tanh⁡x)=sech2⁡x

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

dydx=ddx(14sinh⁡x)=14ddx(sinh⁡x)=14cosh⁡x.

q-95231.name: Question 2
q-95231.worked_solution:
First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic hyperbolic functions:

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sinh}⁡x)=\operatorname{cosh}⁡x,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x)={sech}^{2}⁡x
$$

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\operatorname{sinh}⁡x+3\operatorname{cosh}⁡x) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sinh}⁡x)+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡x) \\  & =2\operatorname{cosh}⁡x+3\operatorname{sinh}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

q-95670.name: Question 3
q-95670.worked_solution:
First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic hyperbolic functions:

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sinh}⁡x)=\operatorname{cosh}⁡x,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x)={sech}^{2}⁡x
$$

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6\operatorname{cosh}⁡x-\operatorname{tanh}⁡x) \\  & =6\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x) \\  & =6\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-{sech}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

q-95670.html:
Question 3
?

Find the derivative of y=6cosh⁡x−tanh⁡x.

a
6sinh⁡x−sech2⁡x
b
6sinh⁡x+sech⁡x
c
−6sinh⁡x−sech⁡x
d
6sinh⁡x+sech2⁡x
e
−6sinh⁡x−sech2⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic hyperbolic functions:

ddx(sinh⁡x)=cosh⁡x,ddx(cosh⁡x)=sinh⁡x,ddx(tanh⁡x)=sech2⁡x

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

dydx=ddx(6cosh⁡x−tanh⁡x)=6ddx(cosh⁡x)−ddx(tanh⁡x)=6sinh⁡x−sech2⁡x.

q-95671.name: Question 4
q-95671.worked_solution:
First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic hyperbolic functions:

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sinh}⁡x)=\operatorname{cosh}⁡x,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x)={sech}^{2}⁡x
$$

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tanh}⁡x-4\operatorname{sinh}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x)-4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sinh}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{sech}^{2}⁡x-4\operatorname{cosh}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic hyperbolic functions:

ddx(sinh⁡x)=cosh⁡x,ddx(cosh⁡x)=sinh⁡x,ddx(tanh⁡x)=sech2⁡x

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

q-95672.name: Question 5
q-95672.worked_solution:
First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic hyperbolic functions:

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sinh}⁡x)=\operatorname{cosh}⁡x,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x)={sech}^{2}⁡x
$$

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-14\operatorname{tanh}⁡x) \\  & =-14\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x) \\  & =-14{sech}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

q-165764.name: Question 6
q-165764.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f={e}^{g},\,g=\operatorname{tanh}⁡s,\,s={x}^{2}
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}s}\cdot \frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}={e}^{g},\,\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}s}={sech}^{2}⁡s,\,\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}x}=2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, multiplying the three results together and substituting for $g$ and $s$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & ={e}^{g}\cdot {sech}^{2}⁡s\cdot 2x \\  & ={e}^{\operatorname{tanh}⁡{x}^{2}}\cdot {sech}^{2}⁡{x}^{2}\cdot 2x \\  & =2x{e}^{\operatorname{tanh}⁡{x}^{2}}{sech}^{2}⁡{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-165764.html:
Question 6
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=etanh⁡x2.

a
esech2⁡x2sech2⁡x2
b
2xetanh⁡x2tanh2⁡x2
c
esech2⁡x2
d
2xetanh⁡x2sech2⁡x2
e
2xetanh⁡x2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as a composite function:

f=eg,g=tanh⁡s,s=x2

The chain rule states that

dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx=dfdg⋅dgds⋅dsdx.

Differentiating, we have dfdg=eg,dgds=sech2⁡s,dsdx=2x.

Finally, multiplying the three results together and substituting for g and s gives

dfdx=eg⋅sech2⁡s⋅2x=etanh⁡x2⋅sech2⁡x2⋅2x=2xetanh⁡x2sech2⁡x2.
q-165764.knowledge_point: Differentiating Hyperbolic Functions Using the Chain Rule

q-95683.name: Question 7
q-95683.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=\frac{2}{g},\,g=\operatorname{cosh}⁡x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=-\frac{2}{{g}^{2}},
$$

and 

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x,
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{2}{{g}^{2}}\cdot \operatorname{sinh}⁡x \\  & =-\frac{2}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{sinh}⁡x \\  & =-\frac{2\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the derivative of f(x)=2cosh⁡x.

2cosh⁡xsinh⁡x
b
 2sinh⁡xcosh⁡x
c
 −2tanh⁡x
d
−2cosh2⁡x
e
−2sinh⁡xcosh2⁡x

Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as a composite function:

f=2g,g=cosh⁡x

The chain rule states that

dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx.

Differentiating, we have

dfdg=−2g2,

and

dgdx=sinh⁡x,

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for g gives

dfdx=−2g2⋅sinh⁡x=−2cosh2⁡x⋅sinh⁡x=−2sinh⁡xcosh2⁡x.

q-95686.name: Question 8
q-95686.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=4{g}^{3},\,g=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=12{g}^{2}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cosh}⁡x.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =12{g}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{cosh}⁡x \\  & =12{sinh}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

q-95686.html:
Question 8
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=4sinh3⁡x.

a
−12sinh2⁡xcosh⁡x
b
12sinh2⁡xcosh⁡x
c
12cosh2⁡x
d
12sinh⁡xcosh2⁡x
e
−12cosh2⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as a composite function: f=4g3,g=sinh⁡x

The chain rule states that dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx.

Differentiating, we have dfdg=12g2

and

dgdx=cosh⁡x.

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for g gives dfdx=12g2⋅cosh⁡x=12sinh2⁡xcosh⁡x.
q-95686.knowledge_point: Differentiating Hyperbolic Functions Using the Chain Rule

q-95682.name: Question 9
q-95682.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=\frac{1}{g},\,g=\operatorname{sinh}⁡s,\,s={x}^{3}
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}s}\cdot \frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g} & =-\frac{1}{{g}^{2}},\,\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}s}=\operatorname{cosh}⁡s,\,\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}x}=3{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, multiplying the three results together and substituting for $g$ and $s$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{{g}^{2}}\cdot \operatorname{cosh}⁡s\cdot 3{x}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{{sinh}^{2}⁡{x}^{3}}\cdot \operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{3}\cdot 3{x}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{3}}{{sinh}^{2}⁡{x}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-95682.html:
Question 9
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=1sinh⁡x3.

a
−3x2cosh⁡x3sinh2⁡x3
b
−3x2sinh⁡x3
c
3x2cosh⁡x3sinh⁡x3
d
 −3x2coth⁡x3
e
 3x2tanh⁡x3
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as a composite function:

f=1g,g=sinh⁡s,s=x3

The chain rule states that dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx=dfdg⋅dgds⋅dsdx.

Differentiating, we have dfdg=−1g2,dgds=cosh⁡s,dsdx=3x2.

Finally, multiplying the three results together and substituting for g and s gives

dfdx=−1g2⋅cosh⁡s⋅3x2=−1sinh2⁡x3⋅cosh⁡x3⋅3x2=−3x2cosh⁡x3sinh2⁡x3.
q-95682.knowledge_point: Differentiating Hyperbolic Functions Using the Chain Rule

q-95679.name: Question 10
q-95679.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=\sqrt{g},\,g=\operatorname{cosh}⁡x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{g}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{g}}\cdot \operatorname{sinh}⁡x \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}}\cdot \operatorname{sinh}⁡x \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}{2\sqrt{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-95679.html:
Question 10
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=cosh⁡x.

a
−12cosh⁡x
b
−sinh⁡x2cosh⁡x
c
12sinh⁡x
d
sinh⁡x2cosh⁡x
e
12cosh⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as a composite function:

f=g,g=cosh⁡x

The chain rule states that

dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx.

Differentiating, we have

dfdg=12g,

and

dgdx=sinh⁡x.

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for g gives

dfdx=12g⋅sinh⁡x=12cosh⁡x⋅sinh⁡x=sinh⁡x2cosh⁡x.
q-95679.knowledge_point: Differentiating Hyperbolic Functions Using the Chain Rule

q-95273.name: Question 11
q-95273.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{2}.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{′}\cdot \operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot (\operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{2})^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{x}\cdot \operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot 2x\operatorname{sinh}⁡{x}^{2} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{2}}{x}+2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x\operatorname{sinh}⁡{x}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{x}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{2}+2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\operatorname{sinh}⁡{x}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

q-95273.html:
Question 11
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=ln⁡xcosh⁡x2.

a
cosh⁡x2+2xln⁡xsinh⁡x2
b
1x(cosh⁡x2+2x2ln⁡xsinh⁡x2)
c
1x(cosh⁡x2+2x2sinh⁡x2)
d
1x(cosh⁡x2−2ln⁡xsinh⁡x2)
e
cosh⁡x2−2ln⁡xsinh⁡x2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=ln⁡x and v(x)=cosh⁡x2. So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(ln⁡x)′⋅cosh⁡x2+ln⁡x⋅(cosh⁡x2)′=1x⋅cosh⁡x2+ln⁡x⋅2xsinh⁡x2=cosh⁡x2x+2xln⁡xsinh⁡x2=1x(cosh⁡x2+2x2ln⁡xsinh⁡x2)

q-165768.name: Question 12
q-165768.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)={x}^{4}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{tanh}⁡{x}^{3}.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{′}(x) & =({x}^{4})^{′}\cdot \operatorname{tanh}⁡{x}^{3}+{x}^{4}\cdot (\operatorname{tanh}⁡{x}^{3})^{′} \\  & =4{x}^{3}\cdot \operatorname{tanh}⁡{x}^{3}+{x}^{4}\cdot 3{x}^{2}{sech}^{2}⁡{x}^{3} \\  & =4{x}^{3}\operatorname{tanh}⁡{x}^{3}+3{x}^{6}{sech}^{2}⁡{x}^{3} \\  & ={x}^{3}(4\operatorname{tanh}⁡{x}^{3}+3{x}^{3}{sech}^{2}⁡{x}^{3})\end{aligned}
$$

t′(x)=(x4)′⋅tanh⁡x3+x4⋅(tanh⁡x3)′=4x3⋅tanh⁡x3+x4⋅3x2sech2⁡x3=4x3tanh⁡x3+3x6sech2⁡x3=x3(4tanh⁡x3+3x3sech2⁡x3)

q-95278.name: Question 13
q-95278.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)={e}^{2x}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{w}^{′}(x) & =({e}^{2x})^{′}\cdot \operatorname{cosh}⁡2x+{e}^{2x}\cdot (\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x)^{′} \\  & =2{e}^{2x}\cdot \operatorname{cosh}⁡2x+{e}^{2x}\cdot 2\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x \\  & =2{e}^{2x}\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x+2{e}^{2x}\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x \\  & =2{e}^{2x}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x+\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x)\end{aligned}
$$

q-95278.html:
Question 13
?

Find the derivative of w(x)=e2xcosh⁡2x.

a
4e2xcosh⁡2x
b
2e2xcosh⁡2x+2sinh⁡2x
c
e2x(cosh⁡2x+sinh⁡2x)
d
2e2x(cosh⁡2x+sinh⁡2x)
e
2e2x(cosh⁡2x−sinh⁡2x)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=e2x and v(x)=cosh⁡2x. So, we apply the product rule:

w′(x)=(e2x)′⋅cosh⁡2x+e2x⋅(cosh⁡2x)′=2e2x⋅cosh⁡2x+e2x⋅2sinh⁡2x=2e2xcosh⁡2x+2e2xsinh⁡2x=2e2x(cosh⁡2x+sinh⁡2x)
q-95278.knowledge_point: Differentiating Hyperbolic Functions Using the Product Rule

q-95234.name: Question 14
q-95234.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)={x}^{2}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =({x}^{2})^{′}\cdot \operatorname{sinh}⁡2x+{x}^{2}\cdot (\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x)^{′} \\  & =2x\cdot \operatorname{sinh}⁡2x+{x}^{2}\cdot 2\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x \\  & =2x\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x+2{x}^{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x \\  & =2x(\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x+x\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x)\end{aligned}
$$

q-95234.html:
Question 14
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=x2sinh⁡2x.

a
2x(xcosh⁡2x−sinh⁡2x)
b
2x2cosh⁡2x
c
2x(sinh⁡2x−xcosh⁡2x)
d
2x(sinh⁡2x+xcosh⁡2x)
e
2x2(sinh⁡2x+cosh⁡2x)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=x2 and v(x)=sinh⁡2x. So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(x2)′⋅sinh⁡2x+x2⋅(sinh⁡2x)′=2x⋅sinh⁡2x+x2⋅2cosh⁡2x=2xsinh⁡2x+2x2cosh⁡2x=2x(sinh⁡2x+xcosh⁡2x)
q-95234.knowledge_point: Differentiating Hyperbolic Functions Using the Product Rule

q-165769.name: Question 15
q-165769.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)={e}^{3x}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{sinh}⁡{x}^{4}.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =({e}^{3x})^{′}\cdot \operatorname{sinh}⁡{x}^{4}+{e}^{3x}\cdot (\operatorname{sinh}⁡{x}^{4})^{′} \\  & =3{e}^{3x}\cdot \operatorname{sinh}⁡{x}^{4}+{e}^{3x}\cdot 4{x}^{3}\operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{4} \\  & =3{e}^{3x}\operatorname{sinh}⁡{x}^{4}+4{x}^{3}{e}^{3x}\operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{4} \\  & ={e}^{3x}(3\operatorname{sinh}⁡{x}^{4}+4{x}^{3}\operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{4})\end{aligned}
$$

q-165769.html:
Question 15
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=e3xsinh⁡x4.

a
e3x(3sinh⁡x4+4x3cosh⁡x4)
b
3e3xsinh⁡x4
c
4x3e3xcosh⁡x4
d
e3xsinh⁡x4+x3cosh⁡x4
e
e3x(sinh⁡x4+cosh⁡x4)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=e3x and v(x)=sinh⁡x4. So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(e3x)′⋅sinh⁡x4+e3x⋅(sinh⁡x4)′=3e3x⋅sinh⁡x4+e3x⋅4x3cosh⁡x4=3e3xsinh⁡x4+4x3e3xcosh⁡x4=e3x(3sinh⁡x4+4x3cosh⁡x4)

q-95326.name: Question 16
q-95326.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $t(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{cosh}⁡x$ and $v(x)={e}^{x}.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{t}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)^{′}\cdot {e}^{x}-\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\cdot ({e}^{x})^{′}}{({e}^{x})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{{e}^{2x}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}(\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)}{{e}^{2x}} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{{e}^{x}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

q-95319.name: Question 17
q-95319.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $g(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)={x}^{2}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{cosh}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2})^{′}\cdot \operatorname{cosh}⁡x-{x}^{2}\cdot (\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)^{′}}{(\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{x(2\operatorname{cosh}⁡x-x\operatorname{sinh}⁡x)}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

q-95319.html:
Question 17
?

Find the derivative of g(x)=x2cosh⁡x.

a
x(2cosh⁡x−xsinh⁡x)cosh2⁡x
b
x2(2cosh⁡x+xsinh⁡x)sinh⁡x
c
x(cosh⁡x−xsinh⁡x)cosh⁡x
d
x2(2cosh⁡x+xsinh⁡x)cosh2⁡x
e
x(2cosh⁡x−xsinh⁡x)sinh2⁡x
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for g(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=x2 and v(x)=cosh⁡x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

g′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(x2)′⋅cosh⁡x−x2⋅(cosh⁡x)′(cosh⁡x)2=2xcosh⁡x−x2sinh⁡xcosh2⁡x=x(2cosh⁡x−xsinh⁡x)cosh2⁡x

q-95235.name: Question 18
q-95235.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)={x}^{2}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2})^{′}\cdot \operatorname{sinh}⁡x-{x}^{2}\cdot (\operatorname{sinh}⁡x)^{′}}{(\operatorname{sinh}⁡x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2x\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-{x}^{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{x(2\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x)}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

q-95235.html:
Question 18
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=x2sinh⁡x.

a
 x(2cosh⁡x−xsinh⁡x)sinh2⁡x
b
x(2sinh⁡x−xcosh⁡x)2sinh⁡x
c
 x(2sinh⁡x−xcosh⁡x)cosh⁡x
d
x(2sinh⁡x−xcosh⁡x)sinh2⁡x
e
 x(2sinh⁡x−xcosh⁡x)cosh2⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=x2 and v(x)=sinh⁡x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(x2)′⋅sinh⁡x−x2⋅(sinh⁡x)′(sinh⁡x)2=2xsinh⁡x−x2cosh⁡xsinh2⁡x=x(2sinh⁡x−xcosh⁡x)sinh2⁡x

q-95320.name: Question 19
q-95320.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $w(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)={e}^{x}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{tanh}⁡2x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{w}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{({e}^{x})^{′}\cdot \operatorname{tanh}⁡2x-{e}^{x}\cdot (\operatorname{tanh}⁡2x)^{′}}{(\operatorname{tanh}⁡2x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}\operatorname{tanh}⁡2x-{e}^{x}\cdot 2{sech}^{2}⁡2x}{{tanh}^{2}⁡2x} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}\overset{g(x)}{\overset{⏞}{(\operatorname{tanh}⁡2x-2{sech}^{2}⁡2x)}}}{{tanh}^{2}⁡2x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=\operatorname{tanh}⁡2x-2{sech}^{2}⁡2x.$

q-95320.html:
Question 19
?

If w(x)=extanh⁡2x, then w′(x)=ex⋅g(x)tanh2⁡2x. What is g(x)?

a
tanh⁡2x−2sech⁡2x
b
2sech2⁡x+tanh⁡x
c
2sech2⁡2x−tanh⁡2x
d
tanh⁡2x−2sech2⁡2x
e
tanh⁡2x+2sech2⁡2x
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for w(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=ex and v(x)=tanh⁡2x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

w′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(ex)′⋅tanh⁡2x−ex⋅(tanh⁡2x)′(tanh⁡2x)2=extanh⁡2x−ex⋅2sech2⁡2xtanh2⁡2x=ex(tanh⁡2x−2sech2⁡2x)⏞g(x)tanh2⁡2x

Therefore, g(x)=tanh⁡2x−2sech2⁡2x.
q-95320.knowledge_point: Differentiating Hyperbolic Functions Using the Quotient Rule

q-95321.name: Question 20
q-95321.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $t(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{sinh}⁡x$ and $v(x)=x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{t}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{sinh}⁡x)^{′}\cdot x-\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\cdot (x)^{′}}{(x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x-\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 20
?

Find the derivative of t(x)=sinh⁡xx.

a
cosh⁡x2+2sinh⁡xx2
b
xcosh⁡x−sinh⁡xx2
c
xcosh⁡x+sinh⁡xx2
d
xcosh⁡x−sinh⁡xsinh2⁡x
e
xcosh⁡x−sinh⁡x2x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for t(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=sinh⁡x and v(x)=x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

t′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(sinh⁡x)′⋅x−sinh⁡x⋅(x)′(x)2=xcosh⁡x−sinh⁡xx2
